Q: How do you optimize context cost without discarding rare but decisive evidence?
A: Context optimization should preserve task-critical support under a measured token and latency budget. Deduplicate repeated material, retain decisive exceptions and track source identities through compression. Estimate with the target tokenizer and include instructions, tool schemas, history and output reserve. Greedy selection by relevance alone can discard an expensive but essential qualifying clause. Evaluate answer support and failure slices after truncation or summarization; a smaller prompt is not automatically a better prompt.
Why: Three repeated positive clauses can outrank one longer exclusion. Keeping all three repetitions wastes budget and can produce an incorrect answer even though the selected text has high average relevance.
Risk: Summaries can omit negation, dates, units or attribution that changes the answer.
Trade: Optimize useful evidence per budget rather than only total token reduction.
Try: Compare full and compressed contexts on a case whose answer depends on one exception.
